description: Decodes a video into sampled image frames. The source can be a public video link, a video on a Tapis file system, or a live RTSP/RTSPS stream.

inputs.name: video
inputs.description: A video on the Tapis file system (wire a 'Video File' source node here). Optional: leave it unwired and set the `source` config instead to pull from a public link or an RTSP stream. When BOTH are given the wired port wins — see the `source` description.

source.description: Public video URL (https://host/clip.mp4) or a live stream URL (rtsp://, rtsps://). Used only when the `video` input port is unwired — the job prefers the staged Tapis file whenever one is present, since a connected edge is a more deliberate statement than a config field left over from an earlier edit. Credentials embedded in a stream URL are redacted out of the manifest and the job log.

sampling_mode.description: How `sampling_rate` is read. 'fps' keeps that many frames per second of video (the usual choice — it means the same thing whatever the source's native frame rate is). 'every_n' keeps 1 of every N decoded frames. 'all' keeps every frame and ignores the rate.

sampling_rate.description: Frames kept per second of video in 'fps' mode, or N in 'every_n' mode. Must be > 0 in fps mode; a 10-minute clip at 1.0 yields ~600 frames.

max_frames.description: Stop after this many SAVED frames; 0 means unlimited. Set a real bound for an RTSP source — a live stream never reaches EOF, so extraction otherwise only stops when the stream drops or the job hits maxMinutes.

image_format.description: Frame encoding. 'jpg' is the right default for feeding detection/training steps; 'png' is lossless and much larger.

output_path.description: Where the extracted frames are archived. Leave it EMPTY (the default) to use this run's own archive dir — job_spec._normalize_archive_dir falls back to it rather than archiving into a literal '${output_path}', and that is the only setting under which the `frames`/`manifest` output ports resolve correctly, because _derive_outputs builds port URIs from the run's archive_uri and not from this override. Set it only for a terminal node whose frames you want at a fixed location; to feed frames downstream AND keep a copy somewhere specific, leave this empty and wire `frames` into a 'Write Image Directory' sink instead.

tapis_job.name: extract-frames
tapis_job.description: Decode a video file, public link, or RTSP stream into sampled frames

fileInputs.name: video
fileInputs.description: Dropped entirely when the `video` port is unwired: an unresolved placeholder here would send Tapis off to transfer a file literally named '${video}'. The plain '${video}' sourceUrl (no 'tapis://${system}/' prefix) is deliberate — the port always resolves to a full tapis://system/path URI, and prefixing it again is what job_spec._normalize_file_inputs exists to repair.
